item.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
item.description:
News
Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
November 15, 20265:41 PM ET
By
Ava Pukatch
This illustration provided by NASA depicts Voyager 1.
AP/NASA
hide caption
toggle caption i
AP/NASA
NASA's Voyager 1 has traveled farther than anything else that humans have launched into space. On Wednesday, it's set to reach a new milestone: reaching a distance that is one-light day away from Earth.
NASA is celebrating the occasion with the "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day." Calling it a symbolic celebration, NASA is asking the public on Tuesday night to send Voyager's call sign V-G-R into the sky in morse code. Use a flashlight, phone light or anything that can blink a sequence.
If you want to take part:
V - Three quick flashes, one long flash G - Two long flashes, one quick flash R - One quick flash, one long flash, one quick flash
What exactly is a light-day?
A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, or more than 16 billion miles.
This NASA spacecraft has traveled for nearly 50 years, launching Sept. 5, 1977.
Over the course of its mission, Voyager 1 has conducted flybys of Jupiter and Saturn. In 1979, it discovered a faint ring system on Jupiter. In 1980, the spacecraft took detailed photos of Saturn's rings and moons. ...

New Orleans port sues owners of tanker involved in Mississippi crash
November 15, 202612:45 PM ET
By
Ava Pukatch
The American Heritage river cruise paddleboat is seen on its side after being struck by the Atlantic Asphalt tanker ship in the Mississippi River, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, in New Orleans.
Gerald Herbert/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Gerald Herbert/AP
New Orleans port officials filed a lawsuit against the owner and operator of the tanker that crashed into a docked cruise ship in the Mississippi River on Friday.
The Board of Commissioners of the Port of New Orleans is seeking at least $1 million in damages from people connected to the tanker, which is called Atlantic Asphalt. The lawsuit also names the tanker's owner, Nave Shipping SA and its management company Thome Ship Management as defendants.
The lawsuit states that at 12:30 p.m. Friday, the Atlantic Asphalt tanker crashed into the American Heritage river cruise paddleboat which was docked at the Thalia Street terminal for disembarkment of passengers.

WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump on Sunday decried a "highly destructive and political decision" from a federal judge after she ordered a two-week delay on renovations at a historic Washington public golf course that he has been trying to redevelop into a championship-level venue.
In a social media post, Trump said his administration will "immediately appeal, on an expedited basis" the temporary restraining order from U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes, which she issued just before East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months.

Many college football teams were in airports Friday on their way to upcoming games when the nationwide ground stop was issued and thousands of flights were canceled. One of the first casualties of a new Florida law that prohibits taxpayer dollars from going toward diversity initiatives is a St. Patrick's Day parade in a beach town that has been celebrating its Irish American community for nearly 60 years.
